title: Embed fanout proration, stale-prefetch refunds, and rate-cap reconciliation
creator: Dana Chen
description:
Problem: Non-chat endpoints that fan out embeddings and structured tool calls are producing incorrect usage charges in several scenarios: (1) speculative/stale prefetches that are later superseded by cached responses still generate full charges, (2) multi-shard fanout (vector shards / rerank partitions) charges are attributed inconsistently when partial success occurs, and (3) tenant-level rate caps are applied before final proration/reconciliation resulting in transient over- or under-charging. These inaccuracies led to a customer incident (SEV-lite) where a batch job incurred 3x expected token/embedding charges after an indexed-rebuild run.

Goal: Implement deterministic proration and refund semantics for embedding/rerank/structured-output fanout so that (a) only work that contributed to a final returned result is billed or billed proportionally, (b) speculative/stale prefetches are automatically refunded, and (c) tenant rate caps are reconciled with post-facto proration to avoid transient quota breaches or unexpected refunds that break accounting invariants.
acceptance_criteria: Metering events include a deterministic provenance tag for every sub-call (shard_id, attempt_id, reason:prefetch|fallback|primary)
Billing pipeline applies proration rules: full-charge for primary contributions, proportional charge for multi-shard merges, zero-charge & refund auto-enqueue for stale prefetches
Rate-cap enforcement reconciles with post-processing: customers never see a final usage > cap after reconciliation; audit log shows pre/post reconciliation delta
End-to-end test coverage: synthetic fanout scenarios (all-success, partial-failures, speculative-prefetch hit, speculative-prefetch stale) show expected invoice line items
Rollout behind feature flag with canary on 5% of tenants and dashboard metrics for charge delta, refund rate, reconciliation lag
implementation_notes:
High-level plan:
1) Provenance metadata: add lightweight provenance token to embeddings and structured-tool invocation requests (uuid per parent request + reason tag). Store minimal provenance in request_events table (request_id, subcall_id, shard_hash, provenance_tag, cost_estimate).
2) Charging model: extend billing worker so it defers final charge until response consolidation step for fanout ops. For merges (e.g., rerank merges) apply a configurable proration policy: priority-based (first-success wins) or score-weighted proportional split. Implement default=score-weighted with opt-out to first-wins via customer flag.
3) Stale prefetch refund: mark prefetches with TTL and cache-generation_id; if final response served from cache that supersedes a prefetch, enqueue refund record and decrement quota in billing ledger via idempotent refund job.
4) Rate-cap reconciliation: keep soft enforcement at admission (reject or queue) but allow reconciliation to correct accounting. Add reconciliation job that ensures final_usage <= cap by applying refunds or marking compensated credits and recording audit entries.
5) Storage/Events: add reconciliation_events stream and new refund_records table. Use idempotency keys to handle retries.
6) Backfill & migration: migration to add provenance columns, backfill for last 30 days for diagnostics, but do not retroactively change charges until reconciliation rules validated in canary.
7) Observability: dashboards for billed_vs_expected, refund_rate_by_tenant, reconciliation_lag, per-request-provenance-drop-rate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Deferring charge to consolidation increases latency on accounting path and could increase memory pressure in billing worker. Mitigation: cap deferral window to 60s and stream partial aggregates to S3 for large fanouts.

Risk: Complex proration rules lead to surprising invoices for customers. Mitigation: expose proration policy in tenant settings and default to conservative score-weighted split; document examples and add an opt-in toggle for legacy first-wins semantics.
Risk: Double-refund or missed-refund due to retries/partial failures. Mitigation: strict idempotency keys on refund job and reconciliation_events; end-to-end test harness simulating retries.

Risk: Edge-case when external billing exports (accounting system) consumes pre-reconciliation data. Mitigation: version billing exports and mark reconciliation windows; coordinate with finance to consume post-reconciliation snapshots for invoicing.
Risk: Increased storage for provenance events. Mitigation: compact provenance payloads (ints for shard_id and small reason enums) and TTL older than 90 days.

Risk: Interaction with Dedicated/Private deployments where on-prem components may enforce different rate-cap semantics. Mitigation: provide a compatibility shim and operator-configurable reconciliation mode in Private deployments.
tasks: Design provenance token schema (DB + event format) - ENG
Extend billing worker to support deferred finalization for fanout ops
Implement refund job with idempotency and ledger adjustments
Add reconciliation job and dashboard metrics
E2E test harness for synthetic fanout scenarios
Canary rollout and monitor for 2 weeks
Documentation and support runbook for refunds and customer comms
